dimensions.reasons: Group A cam_submitted.png and wide_streamside.png clearly depict a wooden gabled mill beside a stream, a large exterior water wheel, a masonry arch bridge, rocks, a lantern, fence, and autumn-colored trees. The required winter variant is also visibly attempted in Group B watermill_winter_hero.png.
issues: The mill reads as a simple single-story shed rather than the requested two-story traditional mill.
The scene lacks a convincing sloped mountain-valley setting and instead sits on a mostly flat, broad ground plane.
The key internal transmission system, stone mill pair, and evidence of the intended motion relationship are not visible.
The stream, foliage, atmosphere, and seasonal treatment are substantially simpler than requested.

dimensions.reasons: The main mill, wheel, stone foundation, and bridge have coherent large-scale support: the wheel axle visibly enters the mill wall in Group A detail_wheel.png, and the bridge has substantial arch and abutment construction in detail_bridge_stream.png.
issues: In the author final watermill_autumn_hero.png and watermill_winter_hero.png, the dark rectangular form below the elevated wooden chute appears unsupported and intersects/obscures the wheel area.
The stream is an abruptly bounded, flat dark plane, with several rocks intersecting it in a visually artificial way.
The winter ice pieces appear as thin, separate rectangular slabs rather than ice naturally attached to the stream edges.

dimensions.reasons: The mill, water wheel, bridge, lantern, and fence are independently recognizable as their intended object types. Group A detail_wheel.png shows a recognizable rim, spokes, hub, axle, and repeated paddle/bucket-like sections, while the stone bridge has a strong readable arch silhouette.
issues: The maple trees are conspicuously low-poly blob canopies with thin simple trunks rather than believable maple crowns.
Autumn foliage is nearly uniform coral-red instead of the requested red, orange, and yellow gradient.
The pale pink roof and uniformly pale weathered boards do not strongly convey aged, moss-stained traditional construction.
The exact count and full bucket form of the requested 20 water buckets cannot be confidently established from the shown wheel.

dimensions.reasons: There is some useful surface detail in the wood and masonry, especially in Group A detail_mill_facade.png, detail_wheel.png, and detail_bridge_stream.png. However, the overall scene remains visibly synthetic rather than a believable autumn valley previs with grounded environmental detail.
issues: The faceted trees, repeated flat ground decals, and highly regular trench-like stream reduce naturalism.
The water appears nearly opaque black and mirror-flat rather than transparent, refractive, or flowing.
Several Group A wide views are very hazy and low-contrast, weakening the intended visual depth and object separation.
No convincing water splash, wheel spray, or visible current is present.

dimensions.reasons: The essential local relationships are sound in Group A cam_submitted.png: the wheel is mounted on the mill alongside the water, the arch bridge crosses the same channel behind it, and the lantern/fence occupy the nearby bank. The submitted camera is broadly a three-quarter view and establishes a readable mill-wheel-bridge grouping.
issues: The stream reads as a narrow, straight engineered trench rather than a roughly 5 m natural creek winding through a valley.
The bridge is positioned very close behind the wheel/mill and competes with, rather than supports, the main silhouette in several views.
The surrounding environment provides little spatial progression into a mountain valley; the background is mostly an indistinct blurred horizon.
The water chute shown in Group B watermill_autumn_hero.png has an unclear connection to the wheel and mill.

dimensions.reasons: The exterior wheel is broadly large enough relative to the mill facade to read as a major water wheel, and the bridge, lantern, rocks, and fence provide some usable scale cues in Group A wide_streamside.png.
issues: Because the mill does not visibly resolve into two levels, its height and wheel-to-building relationship feel less credible than the requested dimensions imply.
The bridge appears unusually massive and visually dominant relative to the compact mill and narrow channel.
Tree crowns are oversized and highly uniform while their trunks are very thin, making their 5–9 m intended scale unconvincing.
The nearly flat terrain does not help communicate the requested 50 m sloped site.

dimensions.reasons: Wood grain and rough stone texture are visible in the Group A close views, and the autumn exterior does have a soft warm directional component. The winter author image changes the roof and ground to a pale snow-covered treatment.
issues: The autumn lighting is washed out and does not convincingly read as a low, 15-degree golden-hour sun with defined warm shadows.
No clear volumetric Tyndall shafts are visible; the haze mostly lowers contrast instead.
Stone and wood have texture but show little convincing localized moss, damp staining, or weathering variation.
Water lacks transparent refraction and flowing/splashing behavior.
In watermill_winter_hero.png, snow is largely a smooth pale cover, while the water wheel has little convincing accumulated snow and the ice reads as separate hard-edged slabs.

dimensions.reasons: The core exterior inventory is substantially present: mill, exterior wheel, bridge, stream, rocks, lantern, fence, trees, an autumn view, a wheel close-up, and a winter variant all appear across Groups A and B.
issues: No visible crown gear, vertical shaft, paired 1.2 m millstones, or proof that the upper millstone rotates while the lower remains fixed is shown.
The mill is not visibly a two-story structure.
The water system lacks visible flowing water, spray at the wheel, transparent refraction, and a convincingly operating overshot feed.
Autumn vegetation lacks the requested varied red-orange-yellow translucent maple foliage and richer scattered ground dressing.
The winter variation does not convincingly place snow on the wheel or naturally form ice along the stream.
No submitted animation frames demonstrate the requested transmission/motion direction.

criteria.criterion: The principal exterior assembly must fully satisfy the specified mill architecture, dimensions, and side-mounted overshot wheel construction.
The native project must contain a continuous, dimensionally correct, mechanically coherent drivetrain from waterwheel to millstones.
The bridge crossing, streambed dressing, bank fixtures, and moss-bearing masonry must form the specified coherent riparian ensemble.
The terrain, maple population, foliage appearance, and ground dressing must jointly form the specified autumn landscape system.
All specified wooden exterior components must share the complete weathered-wood treatment.
The authored water presentation must combine transparent refractive stream optics with readable wheel-area splashing and flow.
criteria.evidence: In watermill_autumn_hero and the Group A stream views, the channel reads as a flat, dark mirror-like sheet with abrupt trench edges; no transparent/refractive view through the water is visible. No splash, spray, wake, or directional water-flow cue is visible around the wheel.

criteria.criterion: The autumn setup must combine the specified native low-angle lighting with its visible warm dusk and Tyndall result.
The actual main-output camera and authored image must satisfy the specified camera setup, composition, depth, and credible-scale goals.
The separate close-up must be a finished authored image that clearly prioritizes the waterwheel.
criteria.evidence: watermill_autumn_wheel_closeup is a distinct, tightly framed authored image in which the waterwheel fills nearly the entire composition, clearly showing its dark weathered wood, layered rim/buckets, spokes, and central axle hub.

criteria.criterion: The third finished image must be a recognizable and fully transformed winter version of the same scene.
criteria.evidence: watermill_winter_hero retains the mill, bridge, wheel, and snowy roof/ground in a cool pale setting, but the wheel remains largely exposed dark brown without readable accumulated snow. The stream-edge treatment consists of thin, separate white slabs that do not clearly read as coherent edge ice.

criteria.criterion: The complete finished-image package must contain all requested openable outputs at the required actual pixel dimensions.
The Blender project must be loadable, editable, organized, correspond to the outputs, and retain the required native render configuration.

notes: The submission successfully establishes a recognizable watermill, wheel, stream, and arch bridge scene, with usable multi-view coverage and a winter attempt. Its main shortcomings are the absent visible mill mechanism, one-story-looking building, artificial water and vegetation, weak valley depth, washed-out presentation, and several unresolved chute/ice geometry issues.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
